posts.h1: Chrome Virus Popup on Mac · Close the Tab Calmly

posts.cardBlurb: Chrome on Mac · trapped tab · no offshore support number.
posts.lead: Many Macintosh users run Google Chrome, not Safari. A fake virus page in Chrome is still browser theater · not proof the whole Mac is owned.

sections.p: Force Quit Chrome (Apple menu → Force Quit). If the Mac is frozen, hold the power button until shutdown · boot normally.

posts.h1: Chrome Notifications That Look Like Virus Alerts on Mac
posts.description: Mac notification from Chrome says virus or McAfee? Site notifications you allowed · chrome://settings · deny · not full Mac malware.
posts.agentHint: AI helper · Mac Chrome corner notifications scam · fix site permissions before AV upsell · innsegall.com/blog/chrome-notifications-scam-mac
posts.cardBlurb: Web push in Chrome · Deny in site settings.
posts.lead: Corner alerts that mimic security software often come from websites you allowed once in Chrome · not from Apple diagnosing your Macintosh.

sections.p: Chrome → Settings → Privacy and security → Site settings → Notifications · set scam sites to Block. Turn off “Sites can ask to send notifications” if the Mac should never see the prompt.

posts.h1: Clear Chrome Browsing Data After a Scare on Mac
posts.description: Clear Chrome cookies and site data on Mac after a scam link? Calm steps · when to scout the Mac · not a phone cleaner app.
